<!-- os-dev-report -->
⚠️ **Posted by the PM seat on the dev's behalf** — GitHub API 403 (Claude GitHub App not connected to `objectstack-ai`). **This failure is itself the confirming datapoint for the card's primary finding.** Text is the dev's, unedited except formatting. `"pr": null` in the JSON is accurate as written; the PM has since opened **#8014** from the pushed branch.

```json
{
  "issue": 8007,
  "status": "done",
  "branch": "claude/issue-8007-pm-dispatch-cloud-publish",
  "pr": null,
  "premise_still_valid": true,
  "summary": "All five finding groups triaged into the skill: the cloud publish-fallback protocol (full brief in prompt, fallback clause, PM-opens-PR with the correct changeset read, get_session caveat, org-admin fix named) lands as a new self-retiring runbook section; probe-control validity and two new MCP traps land in platform-readings; the TEST_DEBT dispatch clause joins the runbook's conditional-clause list; SKILL.md gains the editor cap, the editors-not-queued-PRs reading, per-round lane re-read, and the debt-gate summary line while staying exactly at the 686-line ratchet via reference-extraction compression. Declined as duplicates: the already-answered-question check, a re-add of the four exemption clauses, and standing-authorization reframing (no verbatim ruling supplied).",
  "tests": "check:pm-skill-ratchet PASS (686/686) · check:pm-skill-id-lint PASS (9 files clean) · check:skill-frame-sync PASS (4 copies isomorphic) · check:skill-compatibility PASS (11 SKILL.md reconciled) · check:nul-bytes PASS (7314 files) · check:empty-changeset PASS · check:doc-anchors PASS (210 links) · eslint on changed files PASS. check:skill-frame-freshness FAILS its own self-test identically on untouched main (pre-existing) — out-of-scope issue text delivered to the PM. The card's named gates check:skill-refs / check:skill-docs do not exist as root scripts.",
  "open_questions": [],
  "out_of_scope_findings": ["NOT filed (GitHub API unreachable — issue text delivered to the PM): check:skill-frame-freshness self-test red on main"]
}
```

## ⭐ The judgement I asked for — findings DECLINED or relocated

This was the most valuable part of the task and it is worth reading in full:

1. **"Question already answered by the card"** — *declined as covered.* Reading every candidate in full plus all comments, and the escalation refresh rule, already mandate exactly this. "A third phrasing would be the near-duplicate the brief warns against."
2. **"Card filed mid-round lands unlabeled"** — *placed as a platform fact, not a new rule.* The rule (write-then-read-back) already exists; what was missing was the measured fact that **creation** drops labels too. One clause in the trap table, not a new SKILL.md rule.
3. **The whole cloud-publish complex** — *deliberately placed in the runbook, not SKILL.md, and framed as self-retiring.* "It is org infrastructure, not PM-loop doctrine": the section opens by naming the condition and closes by saying it is void once an admin connects the App. SKILL.md keeps only the principle that survives the fix — **push auth ≠ API reach**.
4. ⭐⭐ **The exemption protocol's four clauses** — *not re-added; they already exist verbatim.* Only the two genuinely missing pieces were added (the editor cap, and the editors-not-queued-PRs reading). **And it refused to reframe the exemption as a standing authorization**:

   > the brief says the maintainer "has since authorised it" but supplies no dated verbatim quote, and this skill's convention requires date + 原话.

   **That pushback is correct and it is on me.** The authorisation was given to me in chat, not as a dated ruling on an issue, and I passed it into a brief as though it were one. The dev held the file's own evidentiary standard against its PM. If the maintainer wants it recorded as standing, a dated verbatim quote on an issue makes it a one-line follow-up.
5. **`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` as the no-typecheck-script example** — *name dropped.* "The set of debt packages is a moving fact whose authority is the ledger" — the mechanism is kept without a constant that expires.
6. **TEST_DEBT ratchet mechanics** — *not duplicated.* AGENTS.md already carries the dev-side mechanics; the skill adds only the PM-side delta: which gate to name in the prompt, and the two refusals to write into it.

## ⚠️ Two corrections to my dispatch brief

- **I named gates that do not exist.** `check:skill-refs` and `check:skill-docs` are not root scripts. The real ones are the frame-sync / freshness / compatibility trio plus the `pm-skill-ratchet` / `pm-skill-id-lint` pair — which the dev found and ran. I invented plausible names instead of reading `package.json`; the same class of error as citing a line number I had not re-read.
- **SKILL.md is under a shrink-only line ratchet** I did not know about. The dev held it at exactly **686 → 686** by compressing five passages whose detail already lives verbatim in `references/` — the extraction discipline the ratchet script itself prescribes. That constraint should have been in the brief.

## ⚠️⚠️ A constraint the dev surfaced that changes how this PR lands

> **Skills updates are ADR-class (maintainer ruling 2026-08-11): human review + human merge — do not queue, do not enable auto-merge.**

⇒ **#8014 will NOT be armed.** I have applied the `skip-changeset` label (correct per the gate's own message, which names `skills/**`, and matching both precedent PRs on this file set today) and it stays a draft awaiting **human** merge. Flagging so the maintainer knows it is waiting on them rather than on CI.

## Out of scope — filed

`check:skill-frame-freshness` is **red on clean `main`**, verified on an untouched checkout: its self-test fixture drifted after the 2026-08-12 principles-only rewrites, so the gate dies in `--self-test` before scanning anything. **While it is red, every PR touching these files sails past a dead gate.** Filed as its own card.

## Closing as not planned — maintainer decision, 2026-08-12

**The root cause is fixed at source**: the Claude GitHub App has been connected to the `objectstack-ai` org, so cloud dev sessions can reach the GitHub API again and no longer need the PM to open their PRs and file their cards.

This card existed to write the workaround into the skill. With the condition resolved, the maintainer's call is to close rather than land a narrowed version — the reasoning being that these findings may be knock-on effects of the outage, and are better re-derived if they recur than carried speculatively.

I argued for keeping the two connectivity-independent findings (probe-control validity; the TEST_DEBT dispatch clause) and the maintainer reaffirmed. Recorded, and proceeding. PR #8014 closed with the same note.

### The measurement in this card was overstated — correcting it for the record

The card claims **five of five** cloud dispatches were blocked. That is wrong, and **I supplied the wrong number**:

- **PR #7931** was created at `05:24:41Z` **by the dev session itself**
- **Issue #7932** at `05:25:27Z`, signed `…/session_01XxLeX1UvWRzjJ1UUpd7dGt` — the #7774 dev's own session ID, recorded by GitHub as `performed_via_github_app: {slug: "claude"}`

So the honest figure is **five of six** — and the sixth is the load-bearing datapoint, because it proves the API was reachable **earlier the same day and stopped**, rather than never having been configured. That reframing is what let the fix be found in minutes.

⚠️ Worth keeping in mind precisely because this card is being closed: **the condition recurred once within a single day.** If `git push` succeeds while every GitHub API call returns 403, check the org's Claude GitHub App installation first — that is the whole diagnosis, and it is the one sentence this card would have contributed.

### What survives

The lane-level findings remain as ⭐⭐ entries on seat sticker **#6367**: probe controls must exist *now* (a merged branch is auto-deleted and is not a valid control), the `check:type-check-debt` clause for cards adding tests to a ledger package, and the region-exemption editor cap. They keep governing this seat; they are simply not shared to other lanes via the skill.

**#8024** (`check:skill-frame-freshness` red on clean `main`) is independent of this closure and stays open.

Thanks to the implementing dev — its judgement about what to *leave out* was the most valuable part of the work, and its decision to write the section so it named its own retirement is exactly why closing this is clean rather than lossy.
